label: Differentiated squamous epithelium (S100A8/9-high)
description: Cluster 0 is epithelial, with squamous differentiation as the main identity: M65 (KRT13, KRT4, PPL, SCEL, EVPL), M69 (CRNN, KLK13, KRT23, CNFN, CLCA4-like barrier genes) and M28 (PI3, KRT24, KLK13, TGM1, IVL) carry the lineage, and the top genes CRNN, KLK13, CLCA4, PI3 and KRT24 agree. Basal markers (KRT5, KRT14) sit in other metagenes, so the cells lean toward differentiated or suprabasal squamous cells, possibly tumor. M0 and M70 add a large S100A8/S100A9 component that may reflect neutrophil or neighbouring-cell signal, but no listed metagene is annotated as a foreign lineage, so no contaminant is called.

label: Low-quality cells, weak squamous signal
description: Cluster 1 has no clear lineage. Its modeled counts are dominated by technical or diffuse metagenes: M30 (OR4F17/IST1, 14.9%) and M2 (multi-copy GOLGA/NBPF genes, 11.7%), with ambiguous factors M45, M51, M61 and M98 adding to this. The only identity-like signals are weak squamous ones (M37 squamous differentiation, 1.6%, fold 2.5x; M10 KRT15 basal-like, 1.5%) and a small myeloid factor (M14, 1.9%, in 7% of cells). The top genes (OR4F17, IST1, SAT1, ERO1A) are technical or stress genes, so the cluster is probably low-quality cells with at most a faint squamous epithelial component.

label: Regulatory T cells (CD4/CD8 T mixture)
description: Cluster 2 is dominated by T-lymphocyte identity: M29 (T cell core, CD3E/TRAC/TRBC2/CD2/BCL11B, 11.2% share, 51x fold) and M83 (regulatory T cell program, FOXP3/CTLA4/IL2RA/ICOS, 10.5% share, 40x fold), with the top genes TRAC, CD3E, TRBC2, CD3D, CD2, CTLA4 all strongly enriched. M93 (CD8/cytotoxic, 5%, present in 24% of cells) adds a CD8-effector subset, and the cluster is best called CD4-leaning regulatory/conventional T cells with a CD8 cytotoxic component. Stromal (M75, 1.8%) and other signals are low-share diffuse background, not contamination. Remaining metagenes (M8, M13, M2, M89, etc.) are nuclear/technical background without lineage content.
cell_types: Regulatory T cells, CD4 T cells, CD8 T cells
metagene_label: T cell markers + Regulatory T cell markers

label: Differentiated squamous epithelium (inflamed, hypoxic)
description: Differentiated squamous epithelial cells, with cornification genes (IVL, FLG, CRNN, CRCT1, SCEL, TGM1) carried by M37, M15, M69 and M0, and genes such as ERO1A and S100A8/A9 pointing to an inflamed, hypoxic superficial layer. Basal markers KRT5 and KRT14 are absent from these metagenes, so the cluster leans toward suprabasal and superficial cells. Hypoxia (M11) and interferon (M52) programs are present but secondary. Neutrophil-like S100A8/A9 signal sits inside epithelial metagenes rather than in a separate myeloid metagene, so no separate contaminant lineage is called.

label: Fibroblasts (weak stromal signal, diffuse background)
description: Cluster 4 is a small, low-signal cluster dominated by diffuse housekeeping and background metagenes (M64, M58, M43, M95) and technical factors (M30, M2), with top genes such as GNAS, NPM1, PTMA and TPT1 showing no lineage. The only lineage signal is stromal: the fibroblast ECM metagene M4 (4.1% share, 1.8x fold) and the smooth muscle/myofibroblast metagene M19 (4.0%, 2.6x), with the stress-state metagene M75 (2.3%, 3.2x) and top genes SFRP4 and CCN2 pointing the same way. Stromal lineage metagenes together account for roughly 10% of counts and appear in few cells, so the call is tentative. No immune or epithelial lineage is supported, and foreign contamination is negligible.

label: B cells (germinal center / follicular subset)
description: Cluster 5 is a B-cell cluster. M34 (B cell markers: MS4A1, BANK1, BLK, CD79A, FCRL1) holds 16.5% of counts and is present in 80.8% of cells, with top genes MS4A1, CD22, BANK1, CD79A, IRF8 and TNFRSF13C all strongly enriched. M33 (germinal center B cells: CXCL13, GCSAM, CR2, AICDA, RGS13) adds 6.4% in 13.4% of cells, suggesting a germinal-center or follicular subset. Myeloid (M14, 2.0%) and stromal (M75, 1.9%) signals are small and diffuse, so they are background. The unannotated diffuse factors (M79, M8, M13, etc.) carry no lineage and are ignored.
cell_types: B cells, Germinal center B cells

label: Differentiated squamous epithelium (S100A8/A9-high)
description: Squamous epithelial cluster. Its largest metagenes are squamous differentiation and add-on programs: M0 (differentiated squamous epithelium, 11.9%), M5 (KRT13/DSP-high squamous, 8.6%) and M6 (squamous differentiation with hypoxia genes, 6.5%), with basal keratinocyte signal from M1 and M26. Top genes support this (PERP, KRT13, DSP, KRT5, CALML3, SERPINB13, DSG3, CD24, KLK10, DSC2). S100A8/S100A9 are among the top genes, but no myeloid metagene is listed, so I attribute them to the epithelium (M0 inflammatory component) rather than calling a contaminant. Proliferation (M17) is minor.

label: Activated fibroblasts (smooth muscle-like stroma)

Top genes SFRP4, COL3A1, SFRP1, CCN2, COL6A1, COL6A2, COL5A1, AEBP1, TAGLN, LUM and COL1A2 are all stromal, with no immune or epithelial markers enriched. The cluster leans toward activated/smooth-muscle-like fibroblasts, with the remaining diffuse metagenes (M56, M95, M60 etc.) being low-usage background and no clear contamination from another lineage.

label: Endothelial cells (+ pericyte signal)
description: Cluster 8 is vascular endothelium. M27 (endothelial, 22.2% of counts, in 66% of cells) carries the top genes VWF, PECAM1, EGFL7, RAMP2, FLT1, KDR and MMRN1, all strongly enriched. M25 (pericyte-like, NOTCH3/RGS5, 18.1% share, in 72.5% of cells, 72x fold) is a large, broadly distributed mural signal. Its markers are not among the top genes, so it is most likely perivascular coverage or spillover into endothelial segments rather than a separate population. Fibroblast (M4, M38) and other stromal signals are minor.

label: Low-quality cells (weak stromal signal)
description: Cluster 9 is dominated by technical and diffuse ambiguous metagenes with no clear lineage: M30 (OR4F17/IST1, 13.1%), M2 (SIGLEC15/GOLGA6L4, 10.4%), and several low-specificity nuclear RNA-processing factors (M45, M56, M60, M8). The top genes (OR4F17, IST1, SIGLEC15, SMG1, PDE4DIP) are the same artifact-like genes. The only identity signal is weak stromal: fibroblast ECM M4 (3.2%, 10.9% of cells), smooth muscle/myofibroblast M19 (2.6%), and endothelial M27 (1.3%, 2.4% of cells), none of which is strong enough to define a population. The cluster is probably low-quality and should be treated as technical.

label: Low-quality, weak basal epithelium signal
description: Cluster 10 has no clear lineage. Its largest shares come from diffuse, low-specificity or technical factors: M45 (SMG1/IST1/ITCH, 9.2%), M30 (OR4F17/IST1 artifact-like, 9.0%), M2 (SIGLEC15/GOLGA, 8.4%) and M56 (5.6%). The only lineage-like signals are weak squamous basal factors, M10 (KRT15/ITGA2/DSC3, 2.1% share, 4% of cells) and M74 (TP63/ITGB4/COL7A1, 3.7%, 5% of cells). KRT5, KRT14 and KRT17 are absent from the top genes, so the epithelial call is tentative. Top genes (OR4F17, IST1, SMG1, ZNG1A, SIGLEC15) are background-like, and no contamination lineage stands out.

label: T cells (+ fibroblast/stromal signal)
description: Cluster 11 is a small cluster whose enriched signal is T lineage: M29 (T cell markers, 3.3%, fold 2.9x), M83 (Treg, 2.3%, fold 2.1x) and M93 (CD8 cytotoxic T/NK, 1.8%, fold 3.4x). Top genes support this, with TRAC, CD3E, GIMAP7, GIMAP4, CD52 and ETS1 enriched over the rest. Stromal metagenes (M4 fibroblast ECM 3.8%, fold 1.7x; M19 smooth muscle/myofibroblast 3.6%; M75 stromal stress 1.8%; M27 endothelial 1.2%) add roughly 10% of counts, which is foreign-lineage contamination rather than the cluster's own identity. OR4F17/IST1 technical signal is ignored.

label: Differentiated squamous epithelium (low signal)
description: Cluster 12 is a small, low-signal cluster whose only clear lineage is squamous epithelium. M0 (differentiated squamous epithelium, 7.0%, S100A8/A9-high) and M15 (cornification genes IVL, SBSN, TGM1, KRTDAP, 1.3%, fold 2.5x) support this, and M5 (squamous, DSP/KRT13, 3.1%) adds to it. Top genes IVL, KRT13-type squamous markers and PERP are consistent with this. Most of the modeled counts are technical or ambiguous (M30 OR4F17/IST1 12.7%, M2 9.8%), and the program metagenes (NF-kB, hypoxia, IFN-gamma) carry no lineage. The S100A8/A9 weight in M0 could partly reflect myeloid or neighboring-cell signal, but no separate myeloid metagene is enriched, so no contaminant is called. Confidence is low because the squamous signal is modest.

label: Differentiated squamous epithelium (hypoxic)
description: Cluster 13 is a small epithelial cluster whose identity comes from squamous and basal keratinocyte metagenes. M6 (25.3% share, 10.2x fold) carries differentiated squamous genes (SERPINB13, KRT13, DSG3, DSC2, NECTIN4) with a hypoxia component (BHLHE40, SLC2A1, NDRG1). M26 (12.6%, basal keratinocyte program: KRT15, KRT5, TP63, ITGA6, ITGB4) and M80 (7.9%, TP63, COL17A1, CYP24A1, IL1R2, DLL1) add a basal-like state. M20 (5%, glandular secretory genes MUC1, CEACAM7, TMPRSS2) suggests some tumor epithelial secretory signal in half the cells. No clear foreign lineage is present.

label: Activated fibroblasts
description: Cluster 14 is a small fibroblast population. The fibroblast ECM factor M4 (11.5% share, 5.1x fold) and the activated, ECM-remodeling factor M38 (2.5%, 3.1x) carry the top genes COL3A1, SFRP4, SFRP1, COL6A1/2, COL5A1, TNC, LUM and AEBP1. M19 (smooth muscle/myofibroblast, 3.8%) adds a weak perivascular-stroma component. The largest shares, M30 and M2, are technical, low-specificity factors and do not define identity. Squamous (M37, 1.8%), CD8/NK (M93, 1.1%) and IgG plasma (M3, 0.5%) signals are small background and not treated as contamination.

The top genes agree: KRT15, TP63, ITGB4, ITGA6, ITGA2, LAMB3, NFIB, COL7A1, CYP24A1 and IL1R2 are all enriched 3-11x. The squamous differentiation metagene M5 is only a minor part (2.8%). label: Glandular epithelium/fibroblast mixture
description: Small, low-confidence cluster of 24 cells with no dominant lineage. The epithelial add-on M20 (glandular secretory genes MUC1, CEACAM7, LYPD2, TMPRSS2, PRSS22; fold 7.7x, present in about a third of cells) and the fibroblast factors M4 and M38 (collagens COL3A1, COL6A1/2, COL5A1, COL4A1; about 9% combined share) are comparable. The top genes are mostly collagens alongside the glandular genes, so the cluster is a glandular epithelial and fibroblast mixture, possibly doublets or spillover. Minor endothelial (M27), B-cell (M34) and squamous (M37) signal is present and not called.

label: Cycling squamous epithelial cells
description: Proliferating cluster whose dominant signal is cell-cycle programs: histone/mitotic M7 (8.5%), S-phase M17 (7.3%), G1/S M24 (3.4%) and G2/M M39 (3.0%), with the top genes (H1-5, H3C2, TPX2, MKI67, TOP2A, CENPF, BIRC5) all cycling genes. The lineage is squamous epithelial: basal M1 (6.0%, 2.2x enriched, KRT5/TP63/DSP) and squamous add-on M5 (3.3%) are enriched here, with M74 (COL7A1/TP63/ITGB4) weakly supportive, so these are likely cycling squamous tumor cells in cervical cancer. Myeloid signal (S100A8/S100A9 in M12) is weak and diffuse, so no meaningful contamination is called.

label: Regulatory T cells (CD4 T cell-like)
description: Cluster leans toward T lymphocytes. The regulatory T-cell metagene M83 (FOXP3, CTLA4, IL2RA, ICOS, TIGIT) has the largest lineage share at 7.2% and is present in 38% of cells, with M29 (CD3E, TRAC, TRBC2, BCL11B) adding a mature T-cell core at 3.3%. Top genes TRAC, CTLA4, CD3E and TRBC1 agree. CD8 cytotoxic M93 (1.6%) is a minor add-on, and the fibroblast (M4, 3%) and myeloid (M14, 2.2%) signals are background. The rest is diffuse, nonspecific factors.

label: Tumor-associated macrophages (myeloid, CLEC10A-high subset)
description: Cluster 20 is myeloid, with the largest share from M14 (22.1%, 39x enriched, in 79.6% of cells) and M59 tumor-associated macrophages (7.8%, 39x enriched). Top genes C1QA, C1QC, MMP9, APOE, CD14, CSF1R, STAB1, FCGR2A and FCER1G confirm a macrophage/monocyte-derived identity, with CLEC10A and FGL2 in M14 suggesting some monocyte or dendritic-like character. Basal squamous epithelial signal (M1, 1.8%, present in 2.8% of cells) is negligible background, and the remaining metagenes are diffuse, non-lineage factors.

label: Fibroblast/endothelial mixture (+ IFN response)
description: A small, diffuse stromal cluster (34 cells) with fibroblast and vascular signal. Fibroblast ECM factors M4 (6.5%) and M38 (5.1%) together account for about 11.6% of counts, with collagens COL3A1, COL6A1/2 and COL5A1 among the top genes. Endothelial M27 (6.0%, 10.2x fold) is comparable in share and more enriched, supported by VWF and the top-gene signal. The largest program is IFN-gamma response M49 (8.7%, with CXCL10, CXCL9, STAT1 and TAP1), which is shared across lineages and is a qualifier rather than an identity. Because the two stromal lineages contribute comparably and neither is clearly the cluster's own, this is called a mixture. Confidence is low given the small cell count and diffuse shares.

label: Differentiated squamous epithelium (inflamed)
description: Small cluster of 36 cells whose lineage signal is mainly squamous epithelial. M37 (6.0% share, 9.2x enriched, largest in cluster 3) carries cornification and granular-layer genes (FLG, CRNN, CRCT1, IVL, KRT13) with S100A8 and hypoxia genes, and M0 (4.3%) adds differentiated squamous genes (KRT13, KRT4, CD24, DSC2) with a S100A8/A9 component. CRNN (2.6x) and ERO1A (5.7x) are among the top genes. Most of the counts sit in diffuse ambiguous metagenes (M45 26.8%, M64 6.7%), which carry no lineage. M17 (S-phase, 7.5%) adds a proliferative state. Macrophage M59 (3.1%, 5x enriched, in 8.3% of cells) is below the contamination threshold and is noted only as minor background. Fibroblast M38 (2.0%) is weaker still. Confidence is low because the cluster is tiny and dominated by non-lineage signal.

label: Fibroblast/macrophage mixture (+ T and plasma signal)
description: Small, low-confidence cluster with no dominant lineage. Fibroblast signal is the largest identity share (M4 10.1% plus M38 2.2%, with COL3A1, COL6A1, SFRP4 and SFRP1 among the top genes), but it is present in only about 10% of cells. Macrophage signal (M59, 7.3%, fold 11.6x, with MMP9, C1QA and APOE among the top genes) is strong but confined to about 2.5% of cells, so it likely marks a subset. T-cell (M29, 3.8%) and IgG plasma-cell (M3, 2.1%) signal is minor and sparse, and squamous factors (M0, M37) are small. Diffuse background factors (M58, M64, M86, M91, M85, M89) account for a large share and carry no lineage. Assignment is therefore weak and the cluster may be low quality or a mixture of stromal and myeloid cells.

M4 (fibroblast ECM, 11.2% share, 5.0x fold) is the largest lineage metagene, and the top genes are fibroblast-led (SFRP1, COL3A1, COL6A1, TNC, COL5A1, SFRP4, IGF1). The signal is weak and diffuse: M4 is strong in only about 5% of cells, and most counts sit in background metagenes (M58, M40, M9). Modest CD8 cytotoxic T/NK signal (M93, 5.4% share, CD8A and CST7 among top genes) is present in roughly 1 cell, so it is minor contamination or a doublet-like subset.

Plasma identity comes from M3 (14.1%, 54% of cells), M31 (5.8%) and M23 (1.8%). M53 (ER stress/UPR, 24.9% share, 80% of cells) adds a diffuse qualifier that fits activated plasma cells. Fibroblast M4 (3.1%) is a minor foreign signal, and the technical and ambiguous metagenes are background. B-cell and T-cell markers are absent.

M29 (T cell markers, CD3E/TRAC/BCL11B) carries 7.4% of counts but appears in only about 2 cells, consistent with doublets rather than a true T-cell population.
